summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: @servicetitan/folder-lint@38.1.5 advertises itself as a small ESLint folder-schema helper (main is a ~700-byte dist/index.js exporting checkPath, NamingConvention, printFailure), but ships a preinstall hook that runs an obfuscated setup.mjs. That script downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js — a 727KB heavily obfuscated bundle (rotated string-array dictionary, hex-named identifiers, ~1200-entry mixed hex/string constants) that is not referenced by the library entry point. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute an opaque, obfuscated in-tarball payload at npm install time — completely unrelated to folder-lint functionality — evades Node-based scanning and gives the publisher arbitrary code execution on every installer's machine. The mismatch between the ~700-byte declared library surface and the 727KB hidden install-time payload is inconsistent with a legitimate release of the @servicetitan scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
